headline: Position depends on your travel month, not general migration timing
summary: The migration is always somewhere in the Serengeti-Mara ecosystem. Your positioning depends on when you travel: December-March places you in southern Serengeti for calving; April-May in central Serengeti as herds move northwest; June-July in western Serengeti for Grumeti crossings; August-October in northern Serengeti or Masai Mara for Mara River crossings; November as herds return south. Position first, then choose camps.

assumptions.text: The migration is not an event but a continuous movement. Animals are always somewhere.
Your travel month determines which region you should position in.
Actual timing varies 2-4 weeks annually based on rainfall patterns.

gains: Correct positioning maximizes migration encounter probability
Each season offers different experiences (calving vs crossings)
Flexible dates allow following real-time reports
losses: Fixed dates may not align perfectly with actual herd position
The Serengeti is 14,750 km²; wrong region means missing migration
Timing shifts mean camps booked far ahead may be wrong location
Following the herds requires flexibility in itinerary

change_conditions: If traveling December-March, position in southern Serengeti (Ndutu area) for calving.
If traveling July-October, position in northern Serengeti or Mara for river crossings.
If dates are fixed, adjust expectations to what is likely in your region.
If dates are flexible, book closer to travel and follow current migration reports.
